label: PF Backlog 612
title: language_rule_check misses large new logic added via EDITS to existing shipped Python (should be Go)
body: language_rule_check.py is ADDED-FILE based: it only fails a NEW .py under a shipped root (core/ api/ adapters/). Substantial NEW logic delivered by EDITING an existing shipped .py passes. Evidence: a whole artifact-contract registry engine was added via an edit to core/contracts.py and the gate reported new_shipped_py_violations=0; it was only caught by human review and then moved to go/pfcore/artifact_contracts.go. The rule intent (BI-PF-0387/0388) is that new shipped LOGIC -> Go, regardless of file.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend components/language_rule_check.py from added-file detection to change-surface detection: diff-based logic-growth check on any shipped-root .py (core/, api/, adapters/). Reuse git diff against base ref; flag hunks adding function/class defs or exceeding a net-new-lines threshold unless the corresponding logic is mirrored in Go (go/pfcore/). Emit new_shipped_py_logic_violations with file+hunk metadata.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES: language_rule_check gate runs in CI (already shipped via BI-PF-0387/0388)
RELATED: BI-PF-0394 (Go core provides the target home for moved logic)
conflict_findings: Low conflict risk: only components/language_rule_check.py and its gate test are modified
Potential friction with any in-flight task adding Python under shipped roots
duplication_findings: No existing backlog item covers edit-based Python logic growth; BI-PF-0394 covers the Go core seam but not this gate
BI-PF-0335/0334 are API contract gates; different concern, no logic overlap
analysis.rationale: The gate's intent is logic-based, but implementation is file-addition-based, creating a bypass. Extending the existing checker to diff hunks closes the gap with minimal new surface; no new component needed.
assumptions: Gate runs on a diff with a known base ref
A net-new-lines / def-count threshold can approximate 'substantial logic'
Exemption mechanism (e.g., pf-allow-py-edit marker or Go-mirror manifest) is acceptable
risks: False positives on legitimate small fixes (threshold tuning needed)
Base-ref availability varies across CI contexts
Cannot auto-detect whether logic was mirrored in Go without a mapping convention

Whether gate blocks (fail) or warns (warn-only) initially

context_review.reason: Strong why (evidence, BI-PF-0387/0388) and where (language_rule_check.py, core/contracts.py, go/pfcore), but what/how/approach/AC/verification are all circular restatements of the title. No definition of how to detect 'substantial new logic' in edits — diff-size threshold, new-symbol/AST complexity detection, baseline snapshot, etc. — is left unstated, so an engineer cannot implement without making core design decisions.
